rule: Disable action triggers immediately upon activation to prevent duplicate submissions or purchases from rapid double-tapping.
why: Rapid or impatient double-taps cause unintended duplicate requests, leading to user frustration and state corruption.
example: Button component enters a disabled loading state on first tap: onClick={() => { setLoading(true); submitForm(); }}

rule: Replace raw technical error logs or undefined strings with contextual, human-readable notification toasts.
why: Exposing raw database errors creates cognitive overload and damages product trust.
example: Displaying 'Something went wrong saving your changes. Try again.' instead of 'Error: TypeError: undefined at Object...'

rule: Ensure focused input fields automatically scroll into view above the software keyboard when the virtual keyboard expands.
why: When keyboards obscure input fields, users cannot see what they are typing, leading to input errors and abandonment.
example: Applying scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'center' }) on input focus events within mobile viewports.

principle: Theme State Persistence on Back Navigation
rule: Maintain consistent color token values and contrast ratios across dark and light mode transitions to prevent unreadable text states.
why: Abrupt theme switches can cause foreground text to blend into newly loaded backgrounds, breaking legibility.
example: Using dynamic CSS custom properties (e.g., var(--text-primary)) that update cleanly without orphan color dependencies.

rule: Persist form input states and user entries locally on page or route transitions so data is not lost when hitting the back button.
why: Losing typed inputs upon navigating backward causes severe user friction and forces repetitive data entry.
example: Autosaving form state to sessionStorage or localStorage on input change events.

rule: Replace generic spinners with structural skeleton loaders that mimic the dimensions and layout of the incoming content.
why: Mimicking the final layout shape reduces perceived waiting time and prevents layout shifts when data resolves.
example: Instead of a centered spinner, display grey pulsing rectangular blocks where cards or lists will load.

principle: Immediate Touch Feedback for Interactive Elements
rule: Trigger instant visual state changes (like scale or color shifts) on every tap, executing heavy tasks asynchronously.
why: Immediate visual confirmation reassures the user that their input was registered, eliminating perceived lag.
example: An action button shows a pressed/active state instantly while the network request is handled in the background.

principle: Fixed Primary CTA Positioning in Stepper Flows
rule: Anchor the primary progression button (e.g., 'Continue') to the exact same screen coordinates across every step of an onboarding flow.
why: Maintaining spatial consistency builds muscle memory, allowing users to progress rapidly without visually searching for the button.
example: Pin the primary 'Next' button to the bottom sticky container across all 4 onboarding screens.

rule: Intercept raw system exceptions (404, 500, stack traces) and display an actionable recovery message with clear next steps.
why: Technical error codes cause confusion and erode trust, whereas plain-language instructions guide the user toward recovery.
example: Instead of 'Error 500: SQL Timeout', show 'We're having trouble connecting. Try again in a moment.' with a retry button.

rule: Provide a fully styled, custom 404 error page complete with navigation pathways back to primary site sections rather than falling back to unstyled server defaults.
why: Prevents user disorientation and abandonment when encountering broken URLs or deprecated links by offering immediate re-engagement options.
example: Before: Browser default white screen with 'Server Not Found'. After: A branded illustration, search bar, and direct links to Home, Pricing, and Support.

rule: Convert text-based phone numbers and email addresses into active tel: and mailto: hyperlinks to enable direct device action.
why: Reduces user friction by eliminating the need to manually copy and paste contact details into external applications on mobile devices.
example: Before: Call us at 555-0199 After: Call us at 555-0199

rule: Provide explicit, visible success and error messaging components immediately following user form interactions.
why: Prevents user confusion and uncertainty by confirming system status or clearly highlighting required corrections.
example:
Before: Form clears silently on error.
After: Inline red error alert displays above the submit button stating 'Please enter a valid email address.'

rule: Position the primary conversion action within the initial viewport so it is visible without requiring vertical scrolling.
why: Maximizes conversion potential by capturing immediate user intent before they scroll past the hero section.
example:
Before: CTA placed at the bottom of a long landing page hero.
After: Primary 'Get Started' button anchored directly beside the main hero headline inside the 100vh container.

rule: Implement a sticky bottom bar housing the primary conversion action on mobile viewports.
why: Keeps the primary conversion goal accessible at all times on small screens, preventing the user from needing to scroll back up to convert.
example:
Before: Static CTA that scrolls away with the content.
After: position: fixed; bottom: 0; width: 100%; z-index: 100; container holding a full-width purchase button.

rule: Ensure all interactive UI feedback and state changes execute within 400 milliseconds.
why: Faster response times keep users feeling in control and prevent the application from feeling sluggish or unresponsive.
example: Button press triggers an immediate loading spinner or state change within 200ms rather than a delayed network block.

rule: Ensure all text elements meet minimum contrast ratios against their background to support users with visual impairments.
why: Sufficient contrast prevents eye strain and ensures content is legible for users with low vision or when viewing screens in bright sunlight.
example: Change secondary gray text from #A0A0A0 to #595959 on a white background to achieve a 4.5:1 contrast ratio.

rule: Provide descriptive alt attributes for all meaningful images to support screen reader users.
why: Screen readers rely on alt text to convey the content and function of images to users who cannot see them.
example: Update `` to ``.

rule: Designate one dominant, high-contrast visual action per view to guide user conversion and minimize cognitive load.
why: Multiple competing primary buttons cause decision fatigue and slow down user progression.
example: Style the primary 'Create Account' action as a filled solid brand button while secondary 'Sign In' is styled as a low-emphasis ghost button.

rule: Utilize spring physics curves instead of linear or basic ease-in-out transitions for UI state changes.
why: Spring animations mimic natural real-world physics, making interfaces feel tactile, responsive, and organic.
example: Apply a damping ratio of 0.8 and response time of 300ms to modal popups instead of a static linear fade.

rule: Disable or substitute motion-heavy transitions when the operating system's reduced motion setting is enabled.
why: Abrupt or scaling animations can trigger vestibular disorders, dizziness, or nausea for sensitive users.
example: Wrap expansive zoom transitions in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` queries.
